post_title: The landlord issue in State College should be studied
post_body:
The landlord issue in State College should be studied

I read many horror stories on this subreddit about landlords. I thought I was safe until I tried to renew my lease today. They literally changed my rent after I had signed my lease, and there is no way for me to prove it. And the fact that they will add a bunch of "add-ons" that are like $200+ more than what we expect really taunts me. Seriously I can't believe we are all here just getting screwed by our landlords. The apartments are obnoxiously getting more expensive for living compared to the price of living in State College and us students are getting taken advantage of just to live here.
My apartment rent comes with internet and water. For this lease, they got rid of them in the "we'll pay for it" section. They told me they won't charge for water, but who knows. I am scared they will charge $75 just for water every month. They did that for electricity last year. In the end, we who rent will just get screwed over with an unjustifiable amount compared to the living costs in State College.
what's up w parkway plaza?
it is notoriously bad. i have never lived there nor do i know anyone who has and even i still know that
Currently living there. Not great. They advertised our apartment as a furnished 3 bed, 2 bath for 650 + utilities. Friend's dad signed the lease. I read through all 40 pages and found that we will actually be paying almost 900/mo. The pool doesn't even work, the gym is one singular room with barely any equipment, and the "study lounge" they advertise has a leak so consistent, the floor boards are puffy. It was also very obvious they didnt clean the apartments thoroughly between tenants-- there were crumbs and cat toys still in our apartment. Additionally, they painted our bedroom doors shut, AND didnt use plastic to cover our floors, so there ended up being paint EVERYWHERE on the floors.
Yup. Same here. It is pretty bad. I had to do a seriously deep clean. And they kept increasing rent and slapped on Utilities last year despite doing nothing.
5 years ago it was a shithole, but it was still cheap (under 600 each for a 2 bedroom that included all utilities and parking) but they took away all of the amenities and raised rent.
I raised holy hell with them when they added that "we may or may not charge you for electricity" bullshit two years ago and left. Have many ridiculous stories from that awful place.
well, about 3 weeks ago there was a leak from a hole in the roof or something, but it caused water damage in every single apartment in the building. They put humidifiers in our apartment and then gave us a one day notice that we have to leave our apartment and bring our pets to a hotel they set up, okay! great! they say we'll be here through oct 13th... well.. this weekend is Penn State homecoming and all of the hotels in the area are fully booked, so no we won't. They didn't tell us that, the hotel did. we find out today we have to move into a "temporary apartment" and remove all of our things from our original apartment, this entire time we are paying rent, they promised a per diem that for some reason will only be paid after the hotel visit and we still have no time frame of when they will be done. genuinely sooo frustrating.
Did you sign without reading the lease? Your copy you signed should have the costs you agreed to. It's not like there are 2 different copies of the lease you signed.
I have read. Otherwise, why would I state that my rent had changed after I had signed my lease?
I understand, I may contact the tenants' rights groups. The lease document I saw and signed vs. the lease document (alongside with the signed copy) that is listed on the apartment resident website, are not the same $.
The signing was all done online with no email copies. The copy and the lease are on their resident's website. I was taken aback when I checked my lease copy again only to realize my rent had changed. The website also doesn't put any time stamps on when these were signed (but just the dates) which makes it even more sketchy. The lease I received was definitely not the same as the lease that is on the website.
How is there zero paper trail?
Did it go through a verification platform like DocuSign or Adobe Sign? If so, go to your emails and click the link you used to sign originally; or you can go to DocuSign / Adobe Sign and sign in with your email address and it may still be there.
If theres no verification process and it was done online, you can argue just as much that your signature was forged upon renewal with your signature because theres no verification in the process.
I would definitely first contact tenants rights, see if the university has resources, or a lawyer if it is an issue. A lawyer to write a letter to request the original document signed would be significantly less than youd pay for increased rent.
Did you not get a copy of the lease when you signed it? This is very very illegal and absolutely a lawyers dream for a class action (since they are presumably doing this to the whole building). If a lawyer can prove it, and they probably can, a judge will eviscerate a company for unilaterally changing a contract like that. That's basically criminal fraud as well.Contact a lawyer!
OP said they use Entrata which is a global property management software company that does over $500MM in revenue a year. The digital lease signing platform is called LeaseExecution and 1000% generates a paper trail. It is an entirely separate software company like Yardi that apartment owners subscribe to. As a small part of my job I oversee about 2000 apartments (not in State College) so Im pretty knowledgeable. What OP is alleging is not only super illegal, but also completely impossible.
I would not put it past a slimy company to just lie to their tenants and hope they don't check the lease. Or even put terms in the lease that permit as described, but those terms would be so egregious any court would strike them down and add penalties, or even explicitly illegal according to renter protections. It's not just generically super illegal, it's a flagrant violation of the principals of contract law. And if there's one thing the American justice system defends, it's contract law.
I firmly suspect that the first thing is what happened. OP likely just didnt read the digital version. While slimy, thats 100% legal. You also cant agree to any terms that contravene existing law. You can waive your rights in certain instances but not always.
Compared to last year's lease, I am seeing a lot of irregularities in the lease renewal.
The landlords were terrible 15 years ago when I was there, so it sounds alike nothing has changed. ARPM knew full well most students don't know enough to stand up for themselves and they take full advantage.
I stayed at a complex where at move out they would threaten to tell your parents they smelled weed once unless you paid them a smoke cleaning fee on your own that they won't let your parents know.
Didn't work on me because I had no guarantor. They also tried to charge us all a cleaning fee for dirty common areas when 2 room mates were still living there....
I had a friend who worked for them and they would literally brain storm how to screw students over
State Colleges housing shortage isnt just about individual landlords, its about politics.
Most voters are long-term homeowners, not students, so council tends to favor preserving neighborhood character over new apartments. Zoning, parking mandates, and height caps make dense projects illegal and costly, while Penn State keeps enrollment high without building enough dorms. Nearby townships resist student housing, and theres no regional body pushing for growth.
Demand rises faster than supply, so rents stay high. You can talk about fairness to politicians until youre blue in the face, but the reality is that only outside intervention from Harrisburg could break the collective action problem. And so far, the state GOP doesnt want to give up local control.
Most voters are long-term homeowners, not students, so council tends to favor preserving neighborhood character
This is a mixed truth. As a homeowner in the area, we are continually having to watch homes get snatched up by landlords and converted into rentals and AirBnBs. Those homes don't convert back to "family properties" very easily, if at all. Those who want to become homeowners equally face a shortage of housing.
How did you sign the lease renewal? Docusign? In-person? I find it so wild you didnt receive a copy immediately after signing. Also check your original lease, its pretty common (unfortunately) for landlords or companies to raise rent for every year you renew and lots of things on the renewal can say things like see original lease. I do agree the situation in state college is pretty rough, but I feel like Id be fighting my rent randomly being raised when I KNOW I didnt agree to that
unless I just signed the renewal and assumed the rent would be the same, but didnt actually go through it, and also didnt receive/ask for a copy.
Not sure what you mean by "no way for me to prove it".
If you sign a lease --- the landlord gives you a copy --- and then if anything changes they have committed breach of contract and you can sue them in court over it.
I would reach out to an attorney and the Attorney General. Start establishing a protest and explain your story as you have here. There would be electronic archival versions of what you signed. The landlord is engaging is highly illegal practices. A lawyer would be happy to represent you and fellow tenants against the scumlord.
We arent the only college town/urban area facing the same problem. From NYC to Honolulu, giant corporate landlords (and smaller landlords) are constantly vying to see how much they can make us pay for as little amenities and nice this things as they can. Its a shitty racketeering operation between the school, the developers/landlords/shareholders, and the homeowners and landowners to see how much they can squeeze us for. Then they run to the local governments and the state begging for looser regulations and less tangible benefits to the community and tenants, and they do it all over again.
They do this bc they know students and a lot of renters dont know their rights. But you do have rights!!! Please research pa rent laws so that you can go after them! Most of the time if you call them out with the correct laws they are breaking and threaten small claims court they will back down and stop doing illegal shit. You have to be stern with them, they are just bullies basically, hoping for the best outcome for you
